html:
The Maidu are a Native American people of northeastern California, living in the valleys and foothills of the northern Sierra Nevada and along the Feather and American rivers. The map spells their name Maiou.

They spoke Maiduan languages and lived in villages, eating acorns, salmon, seeds and game. Their neighbours were the Patwin in the Sacramento Valley, the Miwok to the south and the Northern Paiute across the mountains.

Gold was found at Sutter's Mill in 1848 on land of the southern Maidu, or Nisenan. The Gold Rush that followed brought disease, violence and the loss of their rivers. In 1863 soldiers forced hundreds of Maidu on a march to the Round Valley reservation, and many died on the way. Maidu communities live today on small rancherias across the region.
